OpsBot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: Critical - dedicated pool 'sparrow-prod-pool' reporting sustained 503s for tenant sparrow-corp. Autoscaler triggered spin-ups but requests still 5xx. Impact: Sparrow corp (dedicated) ~30% of requests failing intermittently. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-tenant-isolation|dedicated-tenant-isolation>. Please acknowledge and join bridge if needed.

Alex: acknowledged. I'm on it — will take initial triage. Jamal, can you start with health checks on the pool and confirm if this is noisy neighbor or network isolation?

Jamal: I'm pulling metrics. seeing spike in p50/p99 at the frontend and grpcs to the pool showing "deadline exceeded". k8s shows some pods in CrashLoopBackOff on node gpu-12.

Alex: good catch. grabbing pod logs now.

Alex: ```
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l pool=sparrow-prod-pool
kubectl -n redwood logs sparrow-server-7f9b -c redis-proxy
```

Alex: logs show repeated "kv cache write failed: ENETUNREACH" and then downstream 503s. networking team? could be node-level NIC flapping.

Sofia: tagging netops. @mira please prepare a short customer update for Sparrow CSM (Lee) — they are on pager. We need to be explicit about impact, ETA-ish mitigation steps, and whether we'll offer credits.

Mira: noted. Drafting below — please iterate: "Hi Lee, we're investigating intermittent 503s affecting your dedicated pool. We've identified pod-level network errors causing KV cache write failures. We're isolating the tenant and failing traffic to an unaffected hot-standby pool. We'll share an ETA for full recovery within 30 minutes and follow up with an RCA and any applicable credits." Thoughts?

CSM-Lee: that's good. Ask eng to avoid mentioning root cause until RCA, but confirm steps + ETA. Customer wants a one-liner for execs.

Jamal: mitigation plan: 1) cordon node gpu-12 to stop scheduling; 2) eject affected pods (graceful) and let autoscaler replenish on healthy nodes; 3) if failures persist, shift sparrow-corp routing to backup dedicated pool sparrow-standby via routing rule flip. Starting step 1 now.

Alex: I'm on node cordon. Running `kubectl cordon gpu-12` and `kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`.

OpsBot: Bridge created: <https://redwood.incidents/bridges/5067008421|incident-5067008421-bridge>. Pager escalation: EngOncall->Net->Platform.

Jamal: cordon/drain complete, new pods spinning up on gpu-18/gpu-03. initial traffic percentages back down to baseline but still seeing a handful of 503s from older connections.

Alex: re-deployed redis-proxy with increased connect timeouts as a temporary mitigation. patch applied: `redis-proxy: increase connect timeout to 5s`

Sofia: customer update ready to send. @CSM-Lee can you confirm sending?

CSM-Lee: sending now. I'll include the short exec line: "Temporary networking issue in dedicated pool — mitigation in progress; services degraded for ~20% of calls; standby routing enabled if required."

Mira: quick decision point for credits/SLAs — Sparrow is enterprise with 99.9% dedicated SLAs. We should track downtime window from 5067008400 to recovery. If we end up with > SLA breach we will propose pro-rata credits per contract. I'll draft credit calc after we know exact impacted window and token counts.

Jamal: traffic reroute check — running canary to standby. Command: `rdw route update --pool sparrow-prod-pool --fallback sparrow-standby --percent 10`

Alex: canary shows error rate dropping in prod. increasing to 50%.

OpsBot: Automation: Traffic route flip to standby executed at 5067008800 by Alex (manual override).

Jamal: error rate back to normal after 50% shift. Monitoring for 10m.

Sofia: Great. Preparing an exec briefing slide for Sparrow: timeline, customer impact, mitigation steps, next actions, ownership. Draft slide copy below — please edit: "Impact: Intermittent 503s for Sparrow corp between 12:07–12:25 UTC. Mitigation: cordoned problematic node, redeployed proxies, and routed 50% of traffic to standby pool; full recovery at 12:35 UTC. Post-incident actions: RCA + network team retro, add node-level NIC monitoring alerts, and consider automatic standby failover policy for dedicated pools."

Alex: small correction — recovery observed 12:31 UTC when p95 < 1s across the pool.

Mira: RCA scope items: (a) root cause hypothesis: NIC firmware bug causing kernel-level packet drops under high ephemeral connection churn, (b) why autoscaler didn't replenish fast enough, (c) protect dedicated pools with quicker routing fallback and better preemptive evictions.

Sofia: agree. Also include customer-specific offering: one month pro-rata credit + free 24/7 on-call support handoff for 30 days while we validate stability. Recommend legal review.

CSM-Lee: Sparrow asks for an exec call. Can we do a 30-min briefing in 90 mins?

Alex: yes, I'll prep incident timeline and logs. Jamal — can you produce condensed metric charts we can attach?

Jamal: on it. I'll export p50/p95/p99 charts and the route flip event.

OpsBot: NOTE: create post-incident ticket in tracker: RDW-INC-5067008421 and assign to eng-incident.

Mira: I'll start the RCA doc skeleton and link to ticket. Suggested sections: summary, timeline, impact, root cause analysis, mitigations, long-term fixes, customer comms.

Sofia: owner assignments: Alex (tech lead) -> recovery & timeline; Jamal (metrics lead) -> charts & event log; Mira (RCA owner) -> draft RCA; Sofia (customer comms) -> exec slide + credit proposal; CSM-Lee -> schedule call.

Alex: final status: full routing restored at 5067009065 and p95 stable. marking incident as mitigated. Will keep thread open for RCA and comms. :white_check_mark:
